commander.web.workstation_help_common: Use Tab to reach controls and Enter or Space to activate them. A station comes with all of its rights, including direct fire and Sonar audio where it has them; the host can take them away. Pending commands show their result; uncertain weapon commands are never sent again automatically. Return to your station using the station title above.
commander.web.workstation_help_bridge: The chart shows own ship and published tactical reports. Order course and speed in the adjacent controls. Follow centres the chart on own ship; drag to pan, use the wheel or +/− to zoom. Visual lookout is available in Help & reference.
commander.web.workstation_help_sonar: Choose Broadband, LOFAR, DEMON, TMA, Environment or Active above the instrument. The waterfall shows recent receiver measurements with the newest at the top. Select a contact to focus, classify, release or designate it. Receiver, array and analysis controls are beside the plot. Start Live Sonar with its button.
commander.web.workstation_help_weapons: Inspect the observed target, freshness, affiliation and interlock before selecting a release. Set torpedo depth and choose the appropriate weapon. A second deliberate confirmation is required within five seconds. Tubes, reloads and active own assets are shown alongside the chart.
commander.web.workstation_help_damage: Named compartments show flooding in blue and fire in red. Check the compartment state and trend before assigning a repair team. Use the team buttons in the compartment details to assign or withdraw that team.
commander.web.workstation_help_opz: Use the PPI and contact list to select an observation. Classify only station-owned reports; source classifications remain with their producer. Mark reports to create a manual fusion. Radar controls set emissions and scope range. ESSM and chaff fire from this station.
commander.web.workstation_help_radio: Select a receiver channel to inspect and annotate the intercept, and log its bearing. The scope shows every current bearing; logged bearings and the cross-fixes derived from them are listed in the station panel. Fixes require suitable measured geometry from separated observer positions. Received messages run on the teletype.
commander.web.workstation_help_engine: Order a telegraph setting or explicit speed, and enable quiet mode as required. Compare actual speed, RPM, cavitation and noise with the machinery limits. Damage, grounding and quiet mode can limit the achieved speed.
commander.web.workstation_help_helicopte: Launch or return the helicopter, set a waypoint, and lower the dipping sonar while hovering over water. The dip display separates passive bearings from active range/depth fixes and shows dome depth, estimated thermocline, and safe depth limit. Select a dip contact and release its helicopter bearing to OPZ separately from the ship's sonar bearing. Watch fuel and return margin. Torpedo release requires its own target and direct-fire permission.
commander.web.workstation_help_eloka: Select an intercept and examine bearing, frequency, PRF and modulation. Candidate scores and radar correlations are evidence, not automatic identification. An explicit candidate annotation releases the report; clear the annotation to withdraw your assessment.

commander.web.guide_intro: Use the Commander station to share the published tactical picture, record assessments and submit proposals. The local crew remains in control.
commander.web.guide_access_pairing: The host starts the opt-in service and provides a code with three digits followed by three uppercase letters. The displayed code remains valid for additional crew until host revocation or rate-limit rotation. Five failed attempts per rolling minute are allowed across the service. Pairing creates an independent cookie session that can survive a reload.
commander.web.guide_access_grant: Pairing permits observations. Taking a free station enables all of its controls at once, including direct fire and live Sonar audio where the station has them. The host can revoke a station or single rights at any time.
commander.web.guide_access_revoke: The crew can revoke sessions and command permission immediately in F9. Browser Disconnect asks the host to revoke this session, then clears local tactical data even if the request fails. An inactive session expires, a missing presence poll quickly releases station authority, and a changed world revokes access.
commander.web.guide_operations_picture: Operations shows the mission summary, published contact register, north-up chart, own-ship status, defensive inventory, damage and bounded event history. Bearing-only observations are rays, never invented positions, and tracks are not extrapolated between snapshots.
commander.web.guide_operations_local: Selecting a contact, panning, zooming, following own ship and editing an unsubmitted form are browser-local actions. They do not select the crew target or send a command.
commander.web.guide_lookout: Lookout is a separate north-up observation display. It includes published visual fixes for visible surface vessels, surfaced submarines and aircraft; darkness, sea state, land and distance limit detection. Its range control changes only the browser display and does not confirm identity.
commander.web.guide_observations_age: Observation age is time since the latest published measurement. Fix age is time since the latest positioned fix. Older data may remain visible while becoming stale, uncertain or unavailable; a bearing does not supply range.
commander.web.guide_observations_quality: Quality is the current confidence of the published observation, not certainty of identity. Read it with source, age, fix age and bearing or range uncertainty. Missing values stay unavailable rather than being estimated by the browser.
commander.web.guide_observations_annotat: Operator classification and NATO affiliation are manual assessments, not sensor-confirmed truth. They are sent only after Apply, require an assigned station and may be rejected if the contact or crew assessment changed.
commander.web.guide_target_proposal: An eligible observed contact can be proposed as a target. The proposal does not assign the crew target, authorize a weapon or fire. The crew must accept or reject it locally.
commander.web.guide_navigation_proposal: A navigation proposal may contain course, speed or both. Blank fields remain unchanged. Acceptance in F9 or the crew message box is mandatory before helm setpoints change, and bridge, engine and quiet-mode limits still apply.
commander.web.guide_message_box: Pending target and navigation proposals open the crew message box; the simulation keeps running. Target has priority; F8 switches when both are pending, F6 accepts, F7 rejects, and Escape hides the current notice without deciding it. Pending proposals remain available in F9.
commander.web.guide_reconciliation: HTTP queue acknowledgement is not success. The browser waits for the authoritative crew result and locks further actions. If delivery is uncertain, it never resends automatically; Check / resend uses the identical request and ID, no more than once every five seconds, and may apply it for the first time.
commander.web.guide_eloka_esm: The crew's ELOKA station passively retains up to 64 ESM radar intercepts with bearing, uncertainty, observed frequency, PRF, modulation, quality and age. ESM remains active when own radar is off. Assigning a valid emitter annotation explicitly releases a bearing-only report to OPZ; clearing or changing it stops that release and the old report ages normally.
commander.web.guide_eloka_correlation: Emitter candidates use measured signal properties. Radar and sonar correlation uses compatible time, bearing and observed position, never a hidden entity ID. A manually assigned radar type is an operator annotation. Destroyed operations equipment disables ELOKA measurement and control.
commander.web.guide_emcon: The crew controls surface-search and air-search radar emissions separately. Switching a radar off removes that active sensor's new measurements but does not switch off passive ESM. Emitting can make own forces detectable, so the crew must balance radar coverage against EMCON exposure.
commander.web.guide_analyzer_contacts: Contacts is a read-only browser for the packaged unit catalog. Filter profiles and inspect reference dimensions, machinery, systems, a turning 3D model of the class and generated acoustic analysis diagrams.
commander.web.guide_analyzer_limits: Analyzer selection is independent from the observed contact selected in Operations. A catalog profile is not a live observation, classification, crew target or proposal, and browsing it sends no command.
commander.web.guide_security: Use Commander only on a trusted local network. The host explicitly selects a loopback or private IPv4 address. HTTP traffic is unencrypted and the service is not for Internet exposure. The host-only session cookie is inaccessible to scripts; the page retains only bounded session metadata and CSRF protection in memory.
commander.web.guide_reconnect: Reloading resumes a valid station session automatically. The browser retries interrupted snapshot delivery with a bounded delay. While stale, the picture is frozen and all actions are locked; no motion is predicted and old alarm sounds are not replayed. Expired authorization returns to pairing.
commander.web.guide_authority_forbidden: Commander cannot change rules of engagement, save or load, administer Remote Crew or credentials, quit the game, or operate mission and unit editors.
commander.web.guide_authority_summary: Remote authority is limited to the assigned station's allowlisted controls while paired and live. Every action is revalidated against current observations, readiness and station state.

help.note.bridge_noise: Speed means noise: high speed degrades passive sonar and reveals the frigate. Cavitation starts at 15 kn.
help.note.bridge_coast: Coasts: the frigate cannot sail onto land (it is pushed back).
help.note.bridge_tactic: Stopped/4 kn gives the best listening. Sprint in, then go quiet and prosecute tactically.
help.note.passive: Passive sonar provides bearing only (with array- and own-speed-dependent bearing error).
help.note.tma: TMA estimates target position and speed from maneuvers and a bearing series (confidence rises); it does not estimate depth.
help.note.waterfall: Waterfall: newest at top, oldest at bottom. Broadband X is bearing; LOFAR X is frequency. Brightness is relative received level.
help.note.audio_model: Audio and spectra come from the same synthetic listening beam. Multiple sources and own-ship noise may overlap.
help.note.demon: DEMON shows measured modulation, not certain blade rate or identity. FFT windows span up to 2 s; listen for at least 1 s after changing bearing.
help.note.gain: Gain affects display and audio, not detection. D applies band/notch filtering to audio; DEMON analyzes the unfiltered listening beam.
help.note.snr: SNR is based on signal/noise from range, thermocline, sea state, own noise, and towed-array depth.
help.note.shadow: A target below the thermocline is in a shadow zone (lower SNR).
help.note.parallel: HMS, TAS and a lowered VDS operate in parallel; matching bearings corroborate tracks.
help.note.ghost: A large discrepancy between arrays marks a possible ghost contact.
help.note.tas_handling: TAS performance is available only after complete deployment and stabilization. Deployment/retrieval pauses outside 3-12 kn; overspeed may damage TAS.
help.note.vds: The VDS body is unambiguous like the hull array and quieter; lowered below the layer it hears and pings deep targets without the shadow-zone loss. Lowering and recovery take 2 min each and pause outside 3-15 kn or above sea state 5; the faster the ship, the shallower the body (300 m minus 8 m per knot); above 24 kn it is lost.
help.note.tas_depth: Put TAS below the measured thermocline to hear deep targets.
help.note.active: ACTIVE shows stored echo measurements only: age/fading, bearing, range, and measurement uncertainty.
help.note.sonar_tactic: Listen passively first (at low speed), then ping deliberately. A ping is both a weapon and a warning to the submarine operator.
help.note.roe: ROE STD: the target must be located (ping/TMA/buoy) and classified as submarine or warship. ROE FREE requires classification only.
help.note.target_depth: Target depth comes from active ping, not TMA; the wrong depth causes a miss.
help.note.salvo: Salvo doctrine permits at most 2 wire-guided torpedoes in the water.
help.note.weapon_tactic: Obtain depth by ping, then fire. Decoys imitate signatures and may make a contact lose its own frequencies.
help.note.destroyed: DESTROYED means the station is permanently lost.
help.note.sinking: The frigate sinks when floodwater exceeds its reserve buoyancy and capsizes when free-surface water destroys its stability.
help.note.fire: Fire grows with fuel load, spreads through hot bulkheads and is smothered by flooding; teams fight it once they arrive.
help.note.assignment: Teams can be assigned only to repairable damage; an occupied compartment does not displace another team.
help.note.damage_tactic: Prioritize machinery and sonar, then the hull. Assign a team to fire immediately.
help.note.radar: Radar sees surface vessels, aircraft, and ASMs; submerged submarines remain invisible, a raised mast or snorkel only as a bare blip (B or click marks it).
help.note.ais_esm: AIS supplies civilian tracks; passive ESM analysis is available at Electronic Warfare.
help.note.nato: NATO frames: friendly blue, neutral green, hostile red, unknown yellow.
help.note.ciws: CIWS intercepts automatically inside 1.5 NM (limited ammunition).
help.note.jammer: Jammer ASMs beyond 20 NM provide only a HOJ bearing.
help.note.clutter: The antenna sweeps every 4 s; sea clutter grows with sea state and rain attenuates, so a contact may miss a sweep.
help.note.chaff: Chaff lays a drifting cloud that seduces a missile (40% once bloomed) or blinds it briefly; fire early.
help.note.air_defense: Use chaff and maneuver first, then engage with ESSM. VLS cells are scarce.
help.note.hfdf: HFDF gives bearings and frequency of transmitting submarines (+/-8 degrees ground wave, +/-16 sky wave).
help.note.teletype: Teletype carries HQ bulletins, weather, and ROE changes.
help.note.hfdf_map: Logged bearing lines and cross-fixes appear on the chart.
help.note.hfdf_tactic: Combine an HFDF bearing with a sonar bearing for a position cross-fix.
help.note.cavitation: Above 15 kn, cavitation sharply raises noise and degrades passive sonar.
help.note.engine_damage: Damaged machinery caps speed at 15 kn; destroyed machinery caps it at 8 kn.
help.note.noise_range: Noise percentage indicates own detection/revelation range.
help.note.quiet: QUIET reduces own noise but limits speed to 12 kn.
help.note.engine_tactic: Sprint in (FULL/FLANK), then use SLOW to listen.
help.note.helo_stores: HSP-5 has finite buoy and torpedo stores; launches do not replenish them.
help.note.helo_fuel: Hovering burns fuel faster; running out before landing loses HSP-5. Launch and landing wait for a calm deck.
help.note.buoys: PASSIVE buoys give bearings (two crossing buoys give a fix); ACTIVE buoys give range and bearing. Batteries last 60 min.
help.note.helo_roe: The target must be classified as submarine before an air-torpedo attack.
help.note.shared_controls: H/B/D are also available at Weapons. Helicopter dipping sonar has its own contacts, depth control, active ping, and CIC release.
help.note.helo_tactic: Lay a buoy field ahead of the suspected target position, then recall HSP-5 in time.
help.note.eloka_passive: The ESM receiver remains passive and independent of own radar; activating ECM is a separate deliberate transmission.
help.note.eloka_candidates: Candidate radar types are ranked only from observed frequency, PRF, and modulation; ties are not identification.
help.note.eloka_correlation: Radar/sonar links use compatible time, bearing, and observed position, never hidden identity.
help.note.eloka_damage: A destroyed operations center disables ESM; ELOKA shares the existing operations compartment.
help.note.eloka_tactic: Compare candidate fingerprints and independent tracks before entering an operator assignment.

help.sop.title: Standard procedure:
help.sop.bridge.1: Check mission page (1 twice): objective, time limit, area.
help.sop.bridge.2: Transit at FULL, then slow to SLOW or 4-6 kn before the search area.
help.sop.bridge.3: Search: steady legs of 3-5 min, then turn 30-60 degrees so TMA gains range.
help.sop.bridge.4: Keep clear of the coast and shallow water; watch the chart depth.
help.sop.bridge.5: Torpedo inbound: FLANK, turn away beam-on, order Nixie at Weapons.
help.sop.sonar.1: Go slow (4-8 kn) and select HMS; stream the TAS at 3-12 kn (Y) and lower the VDS below the layer at 3-15 kn (Shift+Y).
help.sop.sonar.2: Search BROADBAND for bearing traces; confirm tonals on LOFAR (N notch).
help.sop.sonar.3: Select the contact (Up/Down), lock focus (Enter), check DEMON.
help.sop.sonar.4: Classify (C); after a course change fit a TMA hypothesis (page TMA: Z/X, Ctrl+Z/X, Q) and accept it (K).
help.sop.sonar.5: Need depth or exact range: ping (Shift+A), then release (G) and mark target (M).
help.sop.weapons.1: Take target from sonar (M) or select a contact with Left/Right.
help.sop.weapons.2: Check the readiness line: range fresh, classification, tubes, salvo limit.
help.sop.weapons.3: Set torpedo depth to the pinged target depth (hold Up/Down).
help.sop.weapons.4: Fire (T or Ctrl+Enter); keep the contact fresh so the wire datum updates.
help.sop.weapons.5: Defence: stream the Nixie early (V); launch HSP-5 (H) for buoys and air torpedoes.
help.sop.damage.1: After a hit, read the compartment plan: fire, flooding, destroyed.
help.sop.damage.2: Fire first: select the room (Left/Right) and a free team (Up/Down).
help.sop.damage.3: Assign with Enter; watch progress and heel on the detail page.
help.sop.damage.4: Then flooding in machinery and sonar spaces, then the hull.
help.sop.damage.5: Withdraw teams (Backspace) once a room is stable and reassign.
help.sop.opz.1: Set radar range (PgUp/PgDn); switch radars for EMCON (R / Shift+R).
help.sop.opz.2: Select tracks (Up/Down), classify (C) and set NATO affiliation (F).
help.sop.opz.3: Merge duplicate reports: mark with Space, fuse with L.
help.sop.opz.5: Missile threat: chaff (G), CIWS release (I), then ESSM (E).
help.sop.radio.1: Read the teletype on page 2: HQ orders, weather, ROE changes.
help.sop.radio.2: On HF activity select the signal (Up/Down).
help.sop.radio.3: Log the bearing (Enter); the line appears on the chart.
help.sop.radio.4: Move at least 1 NM and log a second bearing within 300 s.
help.sop.radio.5: Hand the cross-fix to Sonar/Bridge as a search datum.
help.sop.engine.1: Choose the order with Up/Down or +/-; V enters an exact speed.
help.sop.engine.2: Stay below 15 kn while listening: cavitation masks the sonar.
help.sop.engine.3: Switch QUIET (A) for the attack approach (max 12 kn).
help.sop.engine.4: Never exceed 20 kn with the TAS streamed.
help.sop.engine.5: Watch machinery damage: speed limits of 15 or 8 kn apply.
help.sop.helo.1: Check weather limits and fuel; launch HSP-5 (H).
help.sop.helo.2: Place the waypoint ahead of the suspected target (arrow keys).
help.sop.helo.3: Drop a passive buoy line (B); switch ACTIVE (Shift+B) for range.
help.sop.helo.4: Hover and dip (Y), set depth below the layer (U/V), listen or ping (A).
help.sop.helo.5: Classified submarine: mark target (M), drop torpedo (D); recall in time.
help.sop.eloka.1: Watch new intercepts; filter by status, threat and band (F/Shift+F/B).
help.sop.eloka.2: Select an intercept and compare candidate radar types.
help.sop.eloka.3: Annotate the radar type (C); this releases the bearing to CIC.
help.sop.eloka.4: Missile seeker locked: jam (J), choose the technique (Shift+J).
help.sop.eloka.5: Use auto ECM (A) under saturation; jamming is a transmission.

commander.web.phone_intro: Stand the watch with your phone: turn it to look around, then call what you see by voice or by tapping it. Enter the pairing code shown in the game's F9 Remote Crew page.
commander.web.phone_insecure: This page is not on the HTTPS address: the phone gives no gyroscope and no microphone here. Scan the phone QR code in F9 instead (https://…/lookout).
commander.web.phone_not_understood: Not understood. Say e.g. “Ship bearing 040, range 5 miles”.
commander.web.phone_speech_unavailable: This browser has no speech recognition: tap what you see.
commander.web.phone_speech_failed: Speech recognition failed ({error}). Try again or tap the target.
commander.web.phone_mic_denied: Microphone not allowed. Allow it for this page (iPhone: Settings › Apps › Safari › Microphone) or tap the target.
commander.web.phone_speech_service: Speech recognition is switched off on this phone. On an iPhone turn on Siri and Dictation (Settings › General › Keyboard › Enable Dictation), or tap the target.
commander.web.phone_speech_silent: Nothing heard. Tap Speak and talk right away, or tap the target.
commander.web.phone_mic_busy: The microphone is busy or missing. Close apps that use it, or tap the target.
commander.web.phone_speech_network: The phone's speech service cannot be reached (it needs Internet). Tap the target instead.

scenario.breakthrough.title: Breakthrough (submarine)
scenario.breakthrough.brief: Submarine mission. The submarine must slip past the frigate into a goal area about 5 NM beyond the frigate's patrol position; its orders give bearing and range to the goal. The frigate must stop it: sink the submarine or hold it off until the time limit (5 hours).
scenario.breakthrough.win: Frigate: submarine sunk or held off to the time limit
scenario.breakthrough.lose: Submarine reaches the goal area / frigate sunk
scenario.recon.title: Reconnaissance (submarine)
scenario.recon.brief: Submarine mission. The submarine must find the frigate, get it in sight through the periscope and send a situation report by radio while it is in sight. The frigate must prevent the report: sink the submarine or keep it from reporting until the time limit (2 hours).
scenario.recon.win: Frigate: submarine sunk or report prevented to the time limit
scenario.recon.lose: Submarine reports the frigate in sight / frigate sunk
mission.objective.recon: Stop the submarine reporting the frigate
end.reason.boat_broke_through: The submarine broke through to its goal area

end.reason.boat_reported: The submarine reported the frigate by radio

scenario.convoy_attack.title: Convoy attack (submarine)
scenario.convoy_attack.brief: Submarine mission. The frigate escorts a convoy of four merchants on a steady course at 8 kn; the submarine starts ahead of it. The submarine must sink two of them; its torpedoes can take a merchant as well as the frigate. The frigate must protect the convoy: sink the submarine or bring the convoy through the time limit (3 hours).
scenario.convoy_attack.win: Frigate: submarine sunk or convoy brought through the time limit
